name: Clos Topology
summary: A multistage switching topology that provides many parallel paths between endpoints and is widely adapted for scalable data-center networks.

name: Disaggregation
summary: A systems design principle that separates resources that are conventionally colocated so they can be pooled, scaled, or accessed independently.

name: Direct Memory Access
summary: A data-movement mechanism in which a device transfers data to or from memory with limited CPU involvement in the bulk transfer path.

name: Dynamically reconfigurable connectivity
summary: A connectivity model in which physical or circuit-level paths can be changed under control software instead of remaining statically wired.

name: High Bandwidth Memory
summary: A stacked high-bandwidth memory technology placed close to accelerators to provide much greater memory bandwidth than conventional off-package DRAM.

name: In-network aggregation
summary: A collective-communication technique in which network or fabric elements perform part of a reduction or aggregation operation while data is in transit.

name: Latency
summary: The time required for an operation, transfer, or response to progress from a defined start point to a defined completion point.

name: Liquid cooling
summary: A thermal-management approach that transfers heat using a liquid coolant path close to high-power compute components or racks.

name: Open rack standards and form factors
summary: Open rack and chassis form-factor conventions that shape how compute, storage, power, and serviceable hardware are physically organized in a rack.

name: Rail-optimized fabrics
summary: A fabric organization that aligns accelerator or NIC connectivity into repeated rails so communication can exploit locality and predictable paths.

name: Remote Direct Memory Access
summary: A network data-transfer mechanism that allows direct access to registered memory on another system with minimal CPU involvement in the data path.

name: RDMA over Converged Ethernet
summary: An Ethernet-based networking approach that carries RDMA semantics over an Ethernet fabric, commonly used for high-performance cluster communication.

name: Scale-up versus scale-out
summary: The distinction between tightly coupled accelerator expansion inside a system and cluster expansion across nodes, racks, or fabrics.

name: Topology-aware placement
summary: A placement strategy that assigns workloads or communicating ranks with knowledge of physical network locality and topology to reduce communication cost.

name: Torus topology
summary: A multidimensional topology in which nodes connect to neighbors with wraparound links, providing regular paths and scalable local connectivity.
